answer: Work waits on the ember until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the terrace of the next round. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The pulse of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The design leans on staked peer review with spot checks, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
